t: You're on St Martin's Lane, a street in Westminster that runs north from near Trafalgar Square up to Long Acre. It takes its name from the church of St Martin-in-the-Fields, and at its northern end it becomes Monmouth Street. Several people have connections to this street. The poet and painter Anne Killigrew was born here in 1660, and died of smallpox at just twenty-five. The artist and photographer John Samuel Triptree was also born here. Viscount Conway, a soldier and statesman, and the printer Joseph Smeeton both died on this street.
